added_failures_source: Derived from the reviewed run's own gate logs as the node requires. baseline_suite log baseline.log (revision ed6a90c5288feeb4da160cbeeb354661843264d8): 7 failed plus 1 collection ERROR = 8 failing node ids. after_suite log coordinator-head.log (revision a579ad437e9f60e3412a7b4d3cbc5729e0a5852e): 2 failing ids. Head-minus-base set difference = 0 ids, recomputed both with reckon.crew.review.added_failures_from_gate_logs and by hand; the two head failures (test_a_brief_points_rather_than_quotes and test_crew_recovery) also appear in the base log, so this node adds no failing test id.

findings.text: follow-on: shadow() and change_lane() call plan_dispatch with no route and no picker_selection, so once routing.picker is set to route both resolve to "picker" through resolve_dispatch_route and hit plan_dispatch's guard "picker route has no selection" (dispatch.py:4392); the key is therefore unusable on those two paths, and no test covers shadow or change_lane under route mode, so the gap surfaces only when the deferred activation happens.

item_verdicts.diff: read ed6a90c..a579ad43 (7 files, +244/-15): the key is resolved in one place (resolve_dispatch_route) so the CLI conflict check, the availability refusal, plan_dispatch and the run record all read the same effective route, and the generated schema outputs are regenerated in the same commit.
item_verdicts.done_when: all five points hold at a579ad4: (1) flight accepts routing.picker shadow/route with shipped shadow default and dispatch without --route follows it; (2) --route deterministic overrides the key and is recorded in route_override; (3) tests show shadow, picker and deterministic resolutions plus project-layer precedence and each fails at base; (4) docs/state/reckon/flight.yaml is byte-identical at base and head (blob 6c8ce32fbb89e5689d8cb4403d7edbef7f69acea both revisions); (5) the gate is the 155-file list in gate-files.txt at base and head with zero added failure ids.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is to add the routing.picker flight key that switches dispatch between shadow and picker routing, and the diff does exactly that: a PickerMode enum (shadow, route) and RoutingConfig/RoutingConfig.picker slot in reckon/schema/flight.yaml and the regenerated reckon/_flight_schema.py and docs/_shared/flight.schema.json, a shipped shadow default in reckon/schema/flight-defaults.yaml, resolve_dispatch_route in reckon/crew/dispatch.py, a --route choice extended to deterministic in reckon/cli.py, and route/route_override recorded on DispatchPlan and the run record.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits [a579ad43], baseline_suite revision ed6a90c with 8 failing ids and after_suite revision a579ad4 with 2, both completed with EXIT=1; negative_control_log names a mutation that must break the route-by-key tests; the derived added-failure set is empty.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the single commit a579ad43 touches exactly the declared paths docs/_shared/flight.schema.json, reckon/_flight_schema.py, reckon/cli.py, reckon/crew/dispatch.py, reckon/schema/flight-defaults.yaml, reckon/schema/flight.yaml and tests/test_routing_picker_key.py, all inside the node's grant; the granted evidence-fragment and figure paths are unused because the node's deliverable is code plus tests.

justifications.durability: thirteen new cases fail at the base revision (baseline-routing.log: 13 failed) and pass at head (head-routing.log: 13 passed), and the declared mutation falsifies them (negative-control.log: 3 failed, 10 passed), so the key is guarded where it is exercised; but the internal-caller consequence recorded below is guarded by no test at all, so activating route mode crashes shadow() and change_lane() with nothing to catch it.
justifications.evidence: the receipts are concrete and reconcile with the code: base broad gate baseline.log (revision ed6a90c) ends "7 failed, 1831 passed, 3 skipped, 1 warning, 1 error in 1238.86s" EXIT=1 and head coordinator-head.log (revision a579ad4) ends "2 failed, 1847 passed, 5 skipped, 1 warning in 416.70s" EXIT=1, and I independently re-ran tests/test_routing_picker_key.py against the reviewed tree (13 passed in 37.39s, EXIT=0) and recomputed the added-failure set to zero with the review module; the one weakness is the after_suite command_is_partial marker, the coordinator log naming its options and target list but not its full argv.
justifications.fit: the change extends the existing layered flight-config idiom (enum, slot, defaults, provenance) and records route and route_override beside picker_selection in the same run record shape the picker work already used; the commit carries a subject and a body with no attribution and no plan, sprint or version identifier in code, symbols or comments.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the key, its two permissible values, its shipped shadow default, the deterministic switch-back and the recorded override are all present and exercised, but the promise that the resolved route controls dispatch holds only for the CLI dispatch path that supplies a picker selection; shadow() and change_lane() also now resolve the key and pass no selection, so route mode turns those two internal paths into a hard error rather than following the key.
justifications.scope_discipline: exactly the seven declared paths changed and nothing else, the generated schema outputs were regenerated in the same commit rather than left stale, and the project's own docs/state/reckon/flight.yaml is untouched (identical blob at both revisions), which is the node's explicit constraint.
